name: Is an island a bad idea in a really small kitchen, or can I still fit one?

mainEntity.name: Is an island a bad idea in a really small kitchen, or can I still fit one?

acceptedAnswer.text: A small kitchen does not automatically need an island. In many compact rooms, a peninsula, wall-mounted work surface, or improved perimeter storage preserves more comfortable circulation. Elite Remodeling & Design can compare those options during layout development and show the relationship between cabinets, appliances, doors, and walkways in a design visualization. Key factors include room width, seating goals, dishwasher and oven clearances, traffic from adjoining rooms, and whether the island would reduce preparation space. Measure the narrowest passage rather than relying on the room’s overall dimensions. Choose an island only if it adds useful work or storage without making the kitchen difficult to use.
acceptedAnswer.description: An island is worthwhile only if it adds useful work or storage without restricting circulation. A peninsula or improved perimeter layout may work better; the choice depends on room width, appliance clearances, door swings, and traffic between adjoining spaces.
